headline: This AI Plans Experiments, Then Runs the Lab
author: Whoa Wire
text:
This AI Plans Experiments, Then Runs the Lab

Shanghai Jiao Tong University's AutoDNA combines AI planning with robotic lab work. Given a plain-language request, it coordinates more than twenty instrument types. A DNA-storage demonstration recovered its message exactly; another experiment identified and validated a cancer-linked mutation in a clinical sample. Humans still prepare and maintain the platform, replenish supplies, remove waste and sometimes fix hardware errors. The goal is more autonomous labs, not a claim that scientists are obsolete.

Research credits: Mingyu Wu and colleagues, Nature, “An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations,” published Nov 4, 2026. Shanghai Jiao Tong University AutoDNA project. Reporting: Heidi Ledford, Nature News; James Zou, Nature News & Views; Academic Headline/36Kr.
Paper and supplementary-video credit: Wu et al., Nature (2026), Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Footage: real AutoDNA lab video from Supplementary Videos 2, 4, 5 and 6. Original speed labels and explanatory overlays remain in some shots.
